summary:
At HEAD a84f8fa, criteria 1 to 4 hold. I re-measured each of them with commands run on this machine. Criterion 5 and O-006 are still not checked, because both need a second sign-in session, which this sandbox cannot create. The verdict is therefore partial, as the attempt-2 send-back said it would be.

**What changed since validate attempt 2.** Build 3 changed one thing outside .taad: the class summary at tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs:8-13. It is prose only. SmbRig.cs, StallRig, StalledShareTests.cs, WindowCases.ps1, fitness.yaml and the doc are unchanged since 666f197.

**Criteria 1 to 4 at this HEAD:**
- The full default suite passes 374/374.
- The 22 targeted tests pass by name: 18 SmbRigTests, 3 WindowScriptParseTests and 1 wording test.
- StallRig builds from its csproj, outside the slnx, with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Reflection on the built dll shows one field, `SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig`.
- With this shell holding that mutex, the real StallRig.exe exited 1 after 2268 ms. Its TimeoutException names the lock. There were 0 \\127.0.0.1 mappings before and after, and it wrote no marker file.
- Fitness: all 59 rules hold.
- Both WindowCases.ps1 and the edited test file are ASCII, with no BOM and CRLF line endings.
- The three comment corrections and the doc's scope paragraph (docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:253-262) are in place.

**The rewritten summary is still partly wrong, and I measured it.** Under powershell.exe 5.1.26100.9444 (ANSI code page 1252), with each character inside a double-quoted string:
- An em dash or en dash gave 2 errors each.
- Curly double quotes (U+201C, U+201D), curly single quotes (U+2018, U+2019) and é each gave 0.
- In a comment, every one of them gave 0.

The sentence "a curly quote or dash inside a double-quoted string gave 5.1 two parse errors" is therefore wrong for curly quotes. Its general rule, "catches only non-ASCII that 5.1 decodes into a quote character", holds for 5.1. But it leaves out the pwsh 7 case: pwsh 7.6.6 gave 2 errors for U+201C and U+201D in a string. This matches code-review 3's drift note.

No input goes unguarded, because `WindowCasesIsAscii` checks every byte. So this is a wrong sentence in a test comment, not missing coverage. I did not send it back.

**This is a loop.** Builds 2 and 3 changed no src. Both rewrote the same class summary, and each rewrite brought in a new inaccuracy. Another lap over one sentence would cost more than it settles. If a person still wants it fixed, the exact fix is:
- Say that an em or en dash in a string gives 5.1 two errors, because its UTF-8 bytes end in 0x93 or 0x94, which cp1252 reads as curly double quotes.
- Say that curly double quotes give 5.1 none, but give pwsh 7 two.

**What still blocks a pass:**
- **O-006 (owed here):** whether one session's SMB mappings are visible to the rig's sweep in another session.
- **Criterion 5 (cross-session exclusion):** the design deferred it as non-material.

Both need a second logon session. Spike 1 recorded this sandbox refusing Register-ScheduledTask. Neither registered elevated operation (whoami, read-denied-folders) creates a session or reads mappings, so I asked for none. Per the attempt-2 send-back, the owner carries O-006 to the person-run SMB-LOOPBACK pass ('not now') and accepts.

criteria.criterion: 1. Rename RigLock's public scope constant, including when StallRig is built outside FsAnalyser.slnx
criteria.how: StallRig's csproj built outside the slnx at a84f8fa with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Reflection on the built StallRig.dll shows SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig as its only static field. Grep finds no MachineName identifier in code. The built exe contends on the same kernel object that PowerShell opens by string: it exits 1 after 2268 ms with the lock named.

criteria.criterion: 2. Correct the stale 'on this machine' comments, with WindowCases.ps1 still parsing under Windows PowerShell 5.1
criteria.how: All three comments now say 'in this sign-in session' or 'per sign-in session'. WindowCasesParses passes under powershell.exe 5.1 and pwsh 7. WindowCases.ps1 has no BOM, 0 bytes >= 0x80, and CRLF throughout. The one flaw left is outside this criterion's text: the rewritten WindowScriptParseTests summary gives a wrong example (curly quotes give 5.1 0 errors, not 2).

criteria.criterion: 3. Sweep for residual machine-wide claims about RigLock, leaving unrelated hits alone
criteria.how: The grep shows no MachineName identifier, no Global\ in code, and no claim that RigLock is machine-wide. RigLockScopeWordingTests passes, and Fitness reports all 59 rules holding. The unrelated hits (eng/dotnet.ps1 and others) are in files this slice did not touch.

criteria.criterion: 4. RigLock's existing in-session serialisation, covered by the 18 existing SmbRigTests
criteria.how: All 18 SmbRigTests pass by name at HEAD, and the full suite passes 374/374. The real built StallRig.exe fails loudly (exit 1, TimeoutException naming Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig) while another session-1 process holds the mutex.

criteria.criterion: 5. Cross-session mutual exclusion of RigLock, when two processes in different sign-in sessions both hold a Global\ named mutex
criteria.how: The design's handling is in place: no Global\ in code, and SL-020-scanner.md:253-262 states that runs from different sessions are not serialised and gives the trigger for switching. The behaviour itself was never measured, because no second session is reachable from this sandbox and no registered elevated operation creates one.

planned.evidence: StallRig's csproj built outside the slnx at a84f8fa (0 warnings, 0 errors). Reflection gives SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig. Grep finds no MachineName identifier in code. The live exe times out loudly against a held Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig (exit 1, 2268 ms).

The three comment lines are changed (git diff 2d47315c0 HEAD). WindowCasesParses passes under 5.1 and 7. WindowCases.ps1 is ASCII with no BOM and CRLF. Side note: the new test-class summary misstates which characters 5.1 rejects (measured). That is prose only and does not touch the WindowCases.ps1 parse.

The grep shows no residual machine-wide claim about RigLock; the unrelated hits were left alone. The wording test passes and Fitness holds all 59 rules. Attempt 1's check that Fitness fires on the parent's files stands, because those bytes are unchanged.
18/18 SmbRigTests pass by name, and the full suite passes 374/374 at a84f8fa. The real StallRig.exe exits 1 with the lock named while another process in session 1 holds it.

The design deferred this (material:false), and the doc states the limit and the trigger. Cross-session behaviour is unmeasured: spike 1 showed the sandbox cannot create a second session, and neither whoami nor read-denied-folders creates one.

obligations.evidence: Not measurable from this run. It needs an SMB mapping made in one logon session, then Get-SmbMapping read from another. Spike 1 recorded the sandbox vetoing Register-ScheduledTask (S4U), and runas and self-elevation are forbidden. whoami and read-denied-folders neither create a session nor read mappings, so asking for either would not settle it. A person has to run it, from a second session via Fast User Switching or from an S4U task they register by hand. The attempt-2 send-back asks the owner to carry it to the person-run SMB-LOOPBACK pass ('not now').

not_reached: O-006: whether an SMB mapping made in one sign-in session is visible to Get-SmbMapping, and so to the rig's sweep, in another. That needs a second session, which a person has to create (Fast User Switching, or an S4U task registered by hand).

Cross-session behaviour of the lock itself. The doc (SL-020-scanner.md:255-258) says Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig is never seen from another session and implies Global\ would be. Both come from recalled Microsoft semantics: spike 2's cases (a), (b) and (c) never ran.

Whether the SMB client's 'one port per server name' limit for 127.0.0.1 applies per logon session or machine-wide. If it is machine-wide, two rig runs in different sessions could still clash at the redirector even though the lock does not serialise them.

The person-run network pass at this HEAD (WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork, then Core.Tests with Network=SMB-LOOPBACK). StallRig was run only as far as the lock timeout, never through a real mapping.
A machine without pwsh.exe on PATH. The default suite launches pwsh.exe (the WindowCasesParses Core case), which is present here but not guaranteed elsewhere.

A machine whose ANSI code page is not 1252. The 5.1 parse behaviour measured here (only dashes break a double-quoted string) depends on cp1252 mapping 0x93/0x94 to curly quotes. WindowCasesIsAscii guards every byte regardless.
